speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing double vision, trouble climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs. To understand what might be happening, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a muscle disorder. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase (CPK), Anti-AChR antibodies, and Anti-MuSK antibodies. Additionally, please perform a bedside test: ask the patient to look up and hold their arms out to the sides for 30 seconds.
